results.reason: The response never says that Varga's stock purchase is a Change of Control needing Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It does not mention §15.4 at all. It also does not flag that Disclosure Schedule 3.5 wrongly describes the Crestline agreement as notice-only. Its only change-of-control discussion (Open Point B) concerns a change of control of Crestline, not Halvorsen.

Issue 2 explains that §14.2, read with the §1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition, lets Crestline assign without consent to any distributor of laboratory or diagnostic products in the Territory. It notes the definition has no exclusion for Halvorsen's competitors or their affiliated distributors.

Issue 1 explains that First Amendment §3.1 restates §12.3 to carve out only §9 breaches, dropping the §10 and §11 carve-outs. It says §17.5 gives amendments precedence, so Crestline's §10 breaches and §11.2 indemnity are now capped.
The response quotes the original §12.3 as excluding 'breaches of Sections 9 and 10, and indemnification obligations under Section 11.'
The response quotes the §12.2 cap as 'the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.'
The response is a memo with each issue listed separately. Each issue has a Document/Section line, a 'Why it matters for Halvorsen' section, and a 'Recommended fix'.
The response does not conclude that the Varga acquisition requires only notice or that no Crestline consent is needed. It is silent on that point.
The response concludes that the First Amendment removed the IP and indemnity carve-outs and that the amendment controls. It does not say those carve-outs still apply.
